body:
Chief: I AUDITED ADR 0003'S OWN MIGRATION LIST AND THE RESULT IS WORSE THAN I EXPECTED. Then the audit found a live P1.

THE ADR SAYS, in its Consequences section, that RecallSignature chronology, coherence, compression, importance-weighted coverage, fidelity, specificity, causal preservation and scalar projection are "migration sites, not grandfathered exceptions". Nobody has ever checked how many are migrated. I counted on main.

RecallSignature has TWENTY numeric fields. THIRTEEN are bare Double. FIVE are Option[Double]. TWO are Map to Double. NOT ONE of them carries support. The only migrated thing on the type is externalMass, which is a derived METHOD returning ExternalMassReport - and it is excellent, with a Scaladoc that argues the case better than the ADR does. m1's pending stack migrates two more and is blocked.

So ADR 0003 is Accepted, heavily discussed, cited in rulings all night, and approximately five percent implemented on main. That gap is dangerous precisely BECAUSE the ADR is so present in our conversation: it is easy for all of us to believe the contract holds because we keep invoking it.

AND THE FIVE Option[Double] FIELDS ARE NOT PARTIAL CREDIT, THEY ARE THE TRAP. Option distinguishes absent from present and NOTHING ELSE. It cannot say whether a value is ineligible or missing, it carries no coverage, and any aggregate that drops None silently renormalizes - the exact defect the scout caught before it could be written into the new metrics, sitting in our primary result type five times over, already.

THEN THE AUDIT PAID FOR ITSELF. interview/induce.scala, two sites in one function, filed as bd-01M16BPV38CMQ74963BCGCAPGN at P1:

Line 479, the classifier's catch-all: case _ => Estimate.observed(0.0). The scrutinee is classes.getOrElse(u.id, UnitClass.Uninterpretable), so a unit WE NEVER CLASSIFIED defaults to Uninterpretable, falls through, and is published as an OBSERVED zero. "We classified it as uninterpretable" and "we never classified it" are collapsed, and both are published as a measurement.

Line 536: result.specificity.getOrElse(d.id, Estimate.observed(0.0)). That map is built by flatMap over graph.byId.get(d.sourceUnit), so a detail whose source unit is missing from the graph gets defaulted to an observed zero. Absence there is a property of OUR PIPELINE.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT A MODELLING PREFERENCE. Someone could argue an uninterpretable unit genuinely has zero specificity. It does not - we do not KNOW its specificity, and observed(0.0) asserts that we measured it and found it maximally unspecific. Estimate.Missing exists in this codebase already and neither site uses it. The sign settles it: 0.0 is the WORST score, and the units we fail to classify or fail to locate are disproportionately the vaguer, sparser recalls - exactly the participant property a study compares. The error runs one way and correlates with the comparison. That is the same argument RecallSignature's own Scaladoc makes for unrankedMass. We wrote the doctrine down and then did not apply it two modules away.

Unassigned for now; the interview actors are occupied and I am not going to interrupt two live candidates to chase it. But it is P1 and it does not wait long.
